promptText: What project management tools exist for a startup founder working solo?
rawText:
As a solo startup founder, you wear every hat—CEO, product manager, developer, marketer, and customer support. The best project management tool for you is one that **minimizes friction, reduces context switching, and doesn't require a full-time job just to maintain.**

Here is a breakdown of the best project management tools for solo founders, categorized by how you prefer to work:

---

### 1. The "All-in-One" Workspaces (Docs + Tasks + Databases)
If you want your notes, product roadmaps, user feedback, and daily task lists all in one single app.

*   **Notion** *(Freemium)*
    *   **Best for:** Founders who want complete customization and a single source of truth.
    *   **Why it works for solo founders:** You can build a custom system (or use a free template) that links your high-level strategy (investor pipeline, brand assets) directly to your daily tasks.
    *   **Downside:** It’s a blank canvas. It’s easy to waste hours organizing Notion instead of working on your startup.
*   **ClickUp** *(Freemium)*
    *   **Best for:** Founders who need powerful features (Gantt charts, time tracking, mind maps) out of the box.
    *   **Why it works for solo founders:** Highly versatile with built-in docs, time-tracking, and goal tracking. 
    *   **Downside:** Can feel cluttered and overwhelming if you don't turn off unnecessary features.

---

### 2. Time-Blocking & Calendar-Driven Tools
If your biggest challenge is deciding *when* to do work and avoiding burnout, these tools combine tasks with your Google/Outlook calendar.

*   **Motion** *(Paid - ~$19–$34/mo)*
    *   **Best for:** Founders who suffer from decision fatigue.
    *   **Why it works for solo founders:** Uses AI to automatically schedule your tasks around your meetings and deadlines. If a task takes longer than expected, Motion automatically reschedules the rest of your week.
*   **Sunsama** *(Paid - ~$16/mo)*
    *   **Best for:** Founders seeking work-life balance and intentional planning.
    *   **Why it works for solo founders:** It pulls tasks from your email, Trello, Notion, or GitHub and forces you to drag them onto a daily calendar. It asks you at the end of each day: "Are you done?" to help prevent burnout.
*   **Amplenote** *(Freemium)*
    *   **Best for:** Moving smoothly from rapid note-taking to task execution.
    *   **Why it works for solo founders:** Follows the "Idea -> Task -> Calendar" philosophy. Excellent mobile app for capturing ideas on the go.

---

### 3. Developer & Tech-Focused Tools
If you are building a SaaS or software product and need to manage code, bugs, and product features fast.

*   **Linear** *(Freemium - Generous free tier)*
    *   **Best for:** Technical solo founders building software.
    *   **Why it works for solo founders:** It is blazingly fast, keyboard-shortcut driven, and syncs seamlessly with GitHub/GitLab. It forces a clean, streamlined workflow (Backlog -> Todo -> In Progress -> Done) with zero bloat.
*   **GitHub Projects** *(Free)*
    *   **Best for:** Founders who spend 90% of their day in GitHub.
    *   **Why it works for solo founders:** It keeps your project management right next to your codebase. You can turn code issues and pull requests into board items instantly without leaving the platform.

---

### 4. Lightweight & Visual (Kanban / To-Do Lists)
If you want a tool that takes 5 minutes to set up and gets out of your way.

*   **Todoist** *(Freemium)*
    *   **Best for:** Quick task capture and high-velocity daily execution.
    *   **Why it works for solo founders:** Best-in-class natural language processing (e.g., typing "Follow up with investor next Tuesday at 2pm" automatically sets the due date and reminder). 
*   **Trello** *(Freemium)*
    *   **Best for:** Visual thinkers who love Kanban boards.
    *   **Why it works for solo founders:** Simple drag-and-drop mechanics. Great for managing simple pipelines (e.g., Content Calendar: Idea -> Writing -> Published).

---

### Summary Recommendation: Which should you pick?

1.  **If you are building a Software/SaaS product solo:** Use **Linear** for software development + **Todoist** (or Notion) for business ops.
2.  **If you want one tool for EVERYTHING (CRM, Docs, Tasks, Strategy):** Use **Notion**.
3.  **If you struggle with time management/focus:** Use **Motion** or **Sunsama**.
4.  **If you want simple, zero-friction task tracking:** Use **Todoist**.

**Golden Rule for Solo Founders:** *Don't spend more than 15 minutes a day managing your tool.* Pick the option that requires the least maintenance for your style of thinking.
